originalTitle: Election denier Tina Peters to be hired as elections consultant in conservative California county
summary: Shasta county, center of US election denialism movement, set to appoint ex-Colorado clerk who served prison term
content: A northern California county that has become a hotbed of activism for those who sow doubts about the reliability of voting machines plans to hire Tina Peters, the prominent Colorado election denier recently released from prison, to work on elections. Clint Curtis, the top election official in Shasta county, told the Guardian he plans to hire Peters as a consultant to replace Brent Turner, his top deputy, who has been on medical leave. He said Peters would not have access to the county’s voting system and did not directly respond when asked what her responsibilities would be. Plans to hire Peters, who is still on parole and must receive permission to travel outside of Colorado, were first reported by Action News Now. Shasta county, a conservative region home to 182,000 people, has emerged as a center of the US election denialism movement in recent years. In 2023, the county’s governing body unsuccessfully sought to remake the voting process by cutting ties with the voting machine company Dominion Voting Systems and implementing a hand-count system that experts warned would be costly and far less accurate. The MyPillow CEO Mike Lindell, one of the leading promoters of falsehoods about election fraud in the US, said he would support the county’s effort. The state ultimately blocked Shasta’s plans. In addition, several candidates who lost their race for local office have embraced baseless conspiracy theories about election fraud and sued to overturn results. Last year, the Shasta county board of supervisors appointed Curtis, a Florida-based attorney who had never before overseen an elections office, to serve as the county clerk and registrar of voters. Curtis, who opposes the use of voting machines and has long argued US elections are being manipulated, vowed to overhaul the elections and set an example for the rest of the US. But his tenure has been controversial. Earlier this year investigative reports conducted by the county and an outside body concluded that he had created a hostile work environment and made violent threats against workers. Curtis has denied those claims. Last week, the same board that appointed Curtis censured him, and denounced what it described as his “ongoing and flagrant violations” of county personnel rules, pointing to policies preventing elected officials from “making unfounded allegations that have not been investigated”. Curtis accused staff of “sabotaging elections” and said he planned to sue the county, telling the Guardian: “Everything the old staff accused me of is a lie, and we will be able to prove it in court.” Peters, the former top election official in Mesa county, Colorado, was convicted of four felonies and three misdemeanors in 2024 after she allowed an activist affiliated with Lindell to impersonate a county employee and attend an upgrade of the county’s Dominion voting software. The Gateway Pundit, the far-right news website, subsequently published screenshots of sensitive county information after that breach. Peters was released from prison in June after Colorado governor Jared Polis, a Democrat, commuted her nine-year prison sentence. The hiring of Peters is alarming, said Matt Crane, the executive director of the Colorado county clerk’s association. “Tina Peters and others in the election-denial movement appear to have found another weak link in the chain in California,” he said. “The idea that anyone would bring Tina Peters in as an election expert is almost beyond parody. Maybe she’s an expert on leaving ballots sitting in a ballot box for months after an election. Maybe she’s an expert on committing crimes in the process of trying, and completely failing, to prove election fraud.” “When it comes to actually administering secure, lawful elections, Tina Peters is the last person anyone should be looking to for expertise,” he added. Jena Griswold, Colorado’s secretary of state, said in a statement: “Peters was convicted of four felonies and three misdemeanors related to breaching her own voting equipment while county clerk. It is troubling that she would be in a position to have direct influence on election administration.” Securing the release of Peters from prison was a celebrated cause on the right. Even as Donald Trump pardoned those involved with the January 6 attack on the US Capitol and the fake elector scheme in 2020, he could not help Peters because she was only convicted of a state crime. Polis, facing mounting pressure from the federal government to free Peters, eventually commuted her sentence in May, saying it was unfairly harsh. Polis overrode recommendations from his own clemency board in doing so, according to the New York Times, and has been rebuked by the Colorado Democratic party. Since being released from prison, Peters has hit the Maga media circuit and continued to try and undermine faith in American elections. She continues to assert, falsely, that votes were flipped in 2020, and has urged Trump to declare a national emergency ahead of the 2026 midterms, according to the Atlantic. A copy of Peters’s clemency petition, obtained by the Atlantic, said she would not have the ability to commit similar crimes to the ones she was convicted of because she is no longer a clerk. Curtis’s move to hire Peters comes in the final months of his time in office. In June, voters ousted Curtis in favor of Joanna Francescut, a longtime employee of the Shasta county elections office who was serving as the assistant registrar when Curtis fired her after taking over the office. In the same election, Shasta voters backed a measure to require elections to be held in person on a single day and effectively ending vote by mail while also mandating photo ID and a hand-count. The state quickly sued the county and a judge has temporarily blocked the implementation of the measure.
chineseTitle: 选举否认者蒂娜彼得斯将被聘为保守的加州县选举顾问
chineseSummary: 美国选举否认运动中心沙斯塔县将任命曾服刑的科罗拉多州前书记员
chineseContent: 加州北部的一个县已成为那些对投票机可靠性产生怀疑的人激进主义的温床，该县计划聘请最近出狱的科罗拉多州著名选举否认者蒂娜·彼得斯 (Tina Peters) 从事选举工作。沙斯塔县最高选举官员克林特·柯蒂斯告诉《卫报》，他计划聘请彼得斯作为顾问，以取代一直休病假的最高副手布伦特·特纳。他说彼得斯无法进入该县的投票系统，当被问及她的职责是什么时，他没有直接回应。 Action News Now 最先报道了雇用彼得斯的计划，彼得斯仍在假释期间，必须获得科罗拉多州以外旅行的许可。沙斯塔县是一个拥有 182,000 人的保守地区，近年来已成为美国否认选举运动的中心。 2023 年，该县管理机构试图通过切断与投票机公司 Dominion Voting Systems 的联系并实施手工计票系统来重新制定投票流程，但没有成功，专家警告称，该系统成本高昂且准确性低得多。 MyPillow 首席执行官迈克·林德尔 (Mike Lindell) 是美国选举舞弊谎言的主要推动者之一，他表示将支持该县的努力。该州最终阻止了沙斯塔的计划。此外，几名在地方公职竞选中落败的候选人接受了有关选举舞弊的毫无根据的阴谋论，并提起诉讼以推翻选举结果。去年，沙斯塔县监事会任命柯蒂斯（Curtis）担任县书记员和选民登记员，柯蒂斯是佛罗里达州的一名律师，此前从未监督过选举办公室。柯蒂斯反对使用投票机，长期以来一直认为美国选举受到操纵，他发誓要彻底改革投票机。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
